body: Military operations depend on more than getting troops and equipment to the battlefield; they also require a way to bring the wounded out. For decades, the Lockheed Martin C-130 Hercules has fulfilled that role, combining tactical transport with the evacuation of injured personnel from austere locations. Its latest variant, the C-130J, introduced a more automated flight deck that reduced the standard operating crew from five to three: two pilots and a loadmaster. The stretched C-130J-30 adds 15 feet (4.57 meters) of fuselage length, allowing it to carry more patients with medical attendants in an aeromedical evacuation configuration.

The older C-130H typically required a crew of five to six airmen: at a minimum, two pilots, a loadmaster, a flight engineer and a navigator. In the C-130J, the navigator and flight engineer positions are gradually being phased out as their tasks are taken over by the pilots and loadmaster, helped by a glass cockpit with four multifunctional liquid-crystal displays, head-up displays for each pilot and mission computers that monitor aircraft systems. Charles Moore, conversion officer for the 133rd Airlift Wing, noted the new aircraft has an extra pallet position, modern avionics and a newer, stronger propulsion system that lets it fly higher and slightly faster.

The space freed up goes to the aeromedical evacuation teams. The teams consist of two flight nurses and three medical technicians, five people in total, and are considered part of the flight crew. During a typical mission the nurses oversee the mission details, while the medical technicians pack and load more than 1,000 lb (454 kg) of equipment, including bandages, intravenous fluids, regulators, defibrillators and suction units. Lockheed Martin states the C-130J-30 has space for up to 97 litters with medical attendants, turning the Super Hercules into what the company calls an airborne emergency room with roll-on/roll-off pallets and modular compartments.

The record speaks for itself. The C-130J entered service in 1999, and Lockheed Martin has since delivered more than 570 J-family aircraft to 27 countries, logging more than 3 million flight hours. Air Mobility Command states its rapid-response capabilities give wounded personnel an incredible 98 percent survival rate if they reach a hospital quickly and are returned to the United States within three days or less, against 75 percent in Vietnam, when the average wait was 45 days. Major Christine Cardoza, a US Air Force flight nurse with the 379th Expeditionary Aeromedical Evacuation Squadron, put it simply: "the patient's survival rate, I believe, is more than 98%! Being a part of that is an honor in itself."
en.summary: The C-130J needs only three crew, two pilots and a loadmaster, and its stretched C-130J-30 variant makes room for a five-member aeromedical team of two flight nurses and three medical technicians, plus up to 97 litters.
en.title: The C-130J aircraft flies with a crew of three, until aeromedical missions add five more

facts.claim: The C-130J requires only three crew members to operate: two pilots and a loadmaster, while the earlier C-130H typically required five to six.
The stretched C-130J-30 adds 15 feet (4.57 meters) of fuselage length, and Lockheed Martin states it has space for up to 97 litters with medical attendants.
Aeromedical evacuation teams consist of two flight nurses and three medical technicians, and they pack and load more than 1,000 lb (454 kg) of medical equipment.
The C-130J entered service in 1999, and Lockheed Martin has delivered more than 570 J-family aircraft to 27 countries, logging more than 3 million flight hours.

Air Mobility Command states wounded personnel have a 98 percent survival rate if they reach a hospital quickly and are returned to the US within three days or less, against 75 percent in Vietnam with an average of 45 days.
In a March 2013 mission in Afghanistan, a C-130J crew diverted to Bagram Airfield, completing a journey that normally took more than an hour in just 42 minutes.

body: 軍事行動不只要把部隊與裝備送上戰場，也要能把傷者帶出來。數十年來，洛克希德·馬丁C-130大力士一直扮演這個角色，兼具戰術運輸與從簡陋地點撤離傷患的能力。最新改型C-130J導入自動化程度更高的飛航甲板，將標準操作機組從5人減為3人：2名飛行員與1名裝載長。加長型C-130J-30機身多了15英尺（4.57米），得以在航空醫療後送布局下容納更多病患與醫護人員。
較舊的C-130H通常需要5至6名機組人員，至少包括2名飛行員、1名裝載長、1名飛航工程師與1名領航員。C-130J的領航員與飛航工程師職位正逐步取消，任務由飛行員與裝載長接手，背後是配備4具多功能液晶顯示器、每名飛行員皆有抬頭顯示器、任務電腦監控飛機系統的玻璃座艙。第133空運聯隊換裝軍官查爾斯·摩爾指出，新飛機多了一個托盤位置、配備現代航電與更新更強的推進系統，可以飛得更高、稍快一些。
騰出的空間留給了航空醫療後送小組。後送小組由2名飛行護士與3名醫護技術員組成、共5人，被視為機組的一部分。典型任務中，護士負責掌握任務細節，醫護技術員負責打包與裝載逾1,000磅（454公斤）的裝備，包括繃帶、靜脈輸液、調節器、去顫器與抽吸裝置。洛克希德·馬丁表示，C-130J-30可容納多達97副擔架與隨行醫護人員，能以滾裝托盤與模組化隔間變身為空中急診室。
成績說明了一切。C-130J於1999年服役，此後洛克希德·馬丁已向27國交付逾570架J系列飛機，累計飛行逾300萬小時。空中機動司令部表示，若傷者能迅速抵達醫院、並在3天內送回美國，存活率高達98%；相較之下，越戰時期為75%、平均等待45天。美國空軍第379遠征航空醫療後送中隊飛行護士、克莉絲汀·卡多薩少校說，病患存活率她相信超過98%，能參與其中本身就是一種榮譽。
zh.summary: C-130J只需3名機組：2名飛行員與1名裝載長；加長型C-130J-30則騰出空間，容納2名飛行護士與3名醫護技術員組成的5人醫療小組，最多可載97副擔架。
zh.title: C-130J軍機只需3名機組：航空醫療任務再加2名飛行護士與3名醫護
